newsitem.title: FRANCE: Exiled Algerian FIS ejects hardliners in reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Algerian FIS ejects hardliners in reshuffle.

text.p: The leadership in exile of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) said on Monday it had ousted a hardline member from its executive, prompting the departure of one of his allies.

Ferhat Mechouek, a member of the FIS overseas executive, said by telephone his movement's former vice-president Kamerddine Kherbane had been ejected from the leadership two months ago. Another member, Abdellah Anas, resigned in protest two weeks later.
"We are bringing our movement back to the centre. We rid ourselves of people who were pushing too hard," Mechouek said.
In a statement received in Paris, the FIS in exile named its new vice-president as Abdelkrim Ghemati. Its president, Rabah Kebir, remained in place.
It also said it was "ready to cooperate with political parties and national figures devoted to Algeria and its national character toward common political objectives".
Algerian President Liamine Zeroual has proposed parliamentary elections but excluded the FIS from running by adopting a constitutional amendment banning religious parties.
The statement also reiterated an FIS demand that its two top leaders, Abassi Madani and Ali Benhadj, be released from prison in Algeria.

More than 60,000 people have been killed in civil violence in Algeria since Moslem fundamentalist rebels took up arms against the government after the authorities cancelled 1992 elections that the FIS was poised to win.
